title: Runtime admission-control: priority queues + graceful degradation for overload protection
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a multi-layered load-shedding system in the inference runtime that combines priority queues, admission control, and graceful degradation modes to protect latency SLOs during overload and multi-region failover events. This ticket covers design, implementation, testing, and rollout for the core mechanisms used by Hosted API and Redwood Dedicated runtime.

Why: We've observed recurring P99 latency spikes during traffic bursts and cross-region failovers where requests pile up and KV cache pressure increases. Current soft-quotas and autoscaling are insufficient for short-lived overloads; we need deterministic admission control to protect high-priority traffic (e.g., interactive chat) and provide predictable degradation for low-priority workloads (e.g., batch reranking).

Scope: Priority queuing at request ingress, token-budget based admission control, circuit-breaker hooks at model and node level, and graceful degradation modes (truncate, reduce beam/temperature, fallback model). Includes metrics, dashboards, chaos tests, and a conservative rollout with canary config and per-customer override.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime can classify incoming requests into at least three priorities (critical, standard, best-effort) and enforce queue admission policies.
2) Admission control enforces a global and per-node token-budget with configurable thresholds and drops or reroutes requests when budgets are exhausted.
3) Circuit breakers trip when node-level queue latency or token-exhaustion rate crosses configurable SLO thresholds; closed-loop signals to autoscaler and routing layer.
4) Graceful-degradation strategies implemented: response truncation, lower sampling beams, and automatic fallback to cheaper model variant.
5) End-to-end tests simulating 3 failure modes (sudden burst, gradual ramp, cross-region failover) show 95th latency for critical traffic remains within SLO while best-effort traffic is shed.
6) Dashboards and alerting created: per-priority QPS, Q-length, admission-reject-rate, tokens-consumed, circuit-breaker state.
7) Documentation and runbook for oncall with steps to adjust thresholds and revert configs.

implementation_notes:
Decisions so far:
- Use a two-level priority queue: per-route priority tagging (api-key or route metadata) + token-budget enforcement per worker process.
- Admission control uses a leaky-bucket token counter updated on token emission estimate, not per-character parse, to keep overhead low.
- Circuit breakers live at both worker and host levels; worker-level breaker trips faster for loopback protection.
- Graceful degradation order: 1) truncate response 2) reduce sampling/beam 3) fallback to quantized or smaller variant.
Trade-offs:
- Slight added latency for enqueuing (<1ms median) vs large tail reduction during overload.
- In-region failover prefers draining critical queues over accepting new standard requests, which could increase rejected standard requests during region outages.
Open questions:
- How to classify unknown customer traffic by default priority? (default -> standard, with opt-in tags)
- Integration with Dedicated per-tenant SLAs: expose per-tenant override API (follow-up ticket).
progress_updates:
2026-03-02: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Routing, and SRE. Agreed scope and metrics.
2026-03-04: Prototype implemented in local runtime branch: priority tag propagation and simple per-worker queue. Initial unit tests added.
2026-03-07: Design review with PM and SRE. Feedback: add token-based admission to prevent long-running large-context requests starving short ones; include shutdown drain hook. Action: Rafael to update prototype.
2026-03-09: Updated prototype integrates token-estimate admission. Benchmarks: under synthetic 5x qps spike, P99 for critical improved from 950ms -> 210ms.
2026-03-11: Security/code review started for admission module. Identified need to limit per-request metadata parsing for perf.
2026-03-13: Integration tests added to CI that run overload scenario with chaos-region failover (simulated). Found a race condition in circuit-breaker reset logic. Fix in progress.
2026-03-14: Circuit-breaker reset fix implemented (worker-level cooldown) and bench tests passing. Preparing PR for runtime-1.20 branch.
test_plan: Unit tests for enqueue/dequeue logic and token accounting; component tests that drive a local runtime cluster with a traffic generator to simulate priorities; e2e chaos tests: (1) 10s burst at 10x baseline QPS, (2) multi-minute cross-region failover where one region drains and another receives shifted traffic, (3) slow-leaking requests to verify token-budget fairness. Repro scripts: tests/load-shed-scenarios.py. Acceptance gating: CI must pass e2e with SLO assertions before canary rollout.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Internal canary in us-west with 5% of traffic (read-only routes) and conservative thresholds for admission. Monitor metrics for 48h.
Phase 2: Increase to 30% with warnings and emergency kill-switch. Enable graceful-degradation truncation only for best-effort.
Phase 3: Global rollout with per-region thresholds and per-customer overrides for Dedicated customers. Document control plane flags for immediate rollback.
Rollback criteria: critical P99 > SLO for 15 minutes or rejection rate > 5% for critical tier.
dashboards_and_alerting:
Dashboard: Runtime > LoadShedding > Per-priority metrics (QPS, queue-length, reject-rate, tokens/second).
Alerts: 1) critical_p99_latency_violation (P99 > 300ms for critical) 2) admission_reject_surge (>5% critical rejections in 10m) 3) circuit_breaker_churn (>3 state changes per minute).
Runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/Load+Shedding+Runbook
review_feedback:
SRE (Anika Patel): Reinforced need for bounded memory growth in priority queues; suggested soft-spill to disk as future work.
PM (Liam O'Neill): Ensure product exposes customer-visible metrics for Dedicated and an opt-in per-customer control path.
Design (Priya Rao): UX for client error codes when requests are dropped should include suggested retry-after and alternative endpoints.
Action items from review: add metric for per-request estimated tokens, add client error spec (429 with x-retry-after and alternate model hint).
blockers:
1) Need final approval for per-tenant override API from Product and Legal for Dedicated customers (blocked on PM-118).
2) Observability ingestion spike when tracking per-request token estimates — observability team to provide rollup patterns (ENG-4702).
